quest.title: Counterfeit Classics
quest.description: In the Mahavaipulya Chamber, many are those who have been imprisoned within the pages...

chapter.num: A Long Day in the Mountains: Chapter 1
chapter.title: Paradise

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, what kind of stuff do you two write about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just wondering! Paimon got curious all of a sudden.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: I haven't finished my novel yet. It covers the era of the Archon War, when the adeptal arts were scattered across the mortal realm, leading to the development and evolution of three distinct traditions.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Conflict erupted between the Fanghu Sect of the Mountains and the Yuanjiao Sect of the Seas. Ultimately, the three adepti of Jueyun Karst, the masters of its three summits, descended to mediate this divide of earth and tide.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, did this actually happen in real life?

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Probably not. Then again, the stories that never happened are the ones worth writing.

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: And as for Okikuni...

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: He took the entire cast of Liyue's "Yakshas: The Guardian Adepti" and gender-flipped everyone, then retitled it "Chronicles of the Alluring Yakshas Ravishing Enough to Topple a Kingdom."

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: How can anyone stand this? That's not a title, that's a synopsis!

dialogues.speaker: Okikuni
dialogues.text: Oh, come on... It's just a little something I wrote after reading a light novel. Does swapping the genders really take away from how epic and tragic the story is?

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: To be fair, after changing the lineup to two boys and three girls, the intimate bond between the girls makes the sheer scale of the tragic ending feel even more devastating.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Liyue wasn't a thing in my day, of course, but as a Liyue local, I'll give it an 8 out of 10. Now please, never write again.

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: The book is really weird, but it's a fantastic read. It's even piqued my interest in the original Yakshas.
Hello, Raumhilda, and our new friends.
Oh, Dex is here too.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I'm Zeitlind, her sister.
Oh, I see. You two look so alike...

dialogues.speaker: Okikuni
dialogues.text: My name is Okikuni. As later generations would account it, I should be from the era when youkai roamed the lands, before Narukami unified the thundering archipelago.

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: I'm Calcerius. I'm from the Remurian era.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: And I am Yu Huangyi. I come from the era when Shanhui Fort stood at the foot of Mt. Tianheng, and the Guili Assembly had not yet been founded.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Just a heads-up, besides the newcomers from the borderlands, all Remurians are made of rock. Don't freak out when you see them.

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: For the last time, it's "ichorification!" I'll show you "made of rock," you—!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! We've got one person seamlessly switching between three different personas here!

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: That's because we're all stuck inside these pages!

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Quiet, you! If you hadn't gone and rewritten Erinnyes, would we even be in this mess?

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: As I see it, this is clearly on Okikuni!

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: This place is called the Mahavaipulya Chamber. You can call it the Mahavaipulya Hall or the Mahavaipulya Archives, whichever you prefer.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: As you can see, we have been condemned to exile, pressed between these pages.

dialogues.speaker: Okikuni
dialogues.text: Hey, uh... Can you get Dex to restore me first? We can talk after.

talks.objective: Look for clues to liberate the paper people

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: These are... the letters we wrote to each other. My sister and I.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #They must be really personal. Let's not look through them, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: It's no big deal, really. Just family stuff. She was bored at the sanatorium and wrote them to pass the time.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: She wrote about how the air was fresh, how there were old people everywhere, how comfortable it was in the mountains, but also how dull it was.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: She said that she often went to the sanatorium graveyard to read the epitaphs. She wanted to learn the stories of those who never returned home, those who found their final rest upon the mountain instead.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: She wrote that the sanatorium itself was about to be demolished, that she had to emerge from the shadow of the past.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: And then, one day, she wrote to me and said...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: She was going somewhere far away. And that I shouldn't worry.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: No way. Your sister was really upbeat and talkative when she came here.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: ...Then I came to the temple beneath Windrest Peak and saw her gravestone, perched on a lonely mountain, in a strange and distant land.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, Paimon made you talk about the sad stuff again. And she doesn't know how to comfort you either. Sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: You don't have to comfort me. The latter half of life is nothing but a series of farewells.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: ...It's like writing in the sand. Here one moment, scattered by the next.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Apologies. I really didn't know... I never could've guessed that something like this would happen.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: When she arrived, the selection process for elevation was already a mess. Everyone was in low spirits.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Time, which was already at a standstill, lost all meaning then. It turned into true Nothingness.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Her arrival brought a spark of life we hadn't seen in a long time. She was truly a good person.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I'm really sorry to say this, but I didn't ask for your names just now... because I came with the intention of saying goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I didn't plan on meeting anyone new, because I didn't want to say even more goodbyes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We don't really mind! What matters is that we know each other now, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Farewells are the seeds of reunions.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Going on adventures with lively people... It's not so bad.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I never imagined I'd have a chance like this after growing up.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: That's exactly how your sister made us feel, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And now that we've found what Zeitlind lost, we just have to fix the Restoration Core, right?

talks.objective: Use Dex's ability to liberate the paper people

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Amazing! Melanta's control over this area will finally be broken.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: One more thing, Zeitlind...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: What's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: I misspoke a moment ago. I'd like to correct myself.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Living is a grand adventure, and life is a long journey.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I've held on for this long. Where are the good things I was supposed to find?

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: #You met {NICKNAME}, Paimon, and me. And then you came here.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: It might be a complete mess at the moment, but to be chosen to come here and attain eternity is a one-in-a-million chance.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: You said you wanted to stay here a while ago, right? What do you think? Would you like to stay?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: This is a good place.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Everyone lives in harmony. You are all wise and pure of heart.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: We can talk about that later, let's head back first. I wonder how Okikuni and Calcerius are doing.

dialogues.speaker: Okikuni
dialogues.text: You did it! You guys are amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Okikuni
dialogues.text: In terms of strength, you are, at the very least, an entry-level Legion Commander.

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: You say that, but even amongst "entry-level Legion Commanders," you've got golem constructs, arbiters, aspirant arbiters, and arbiter-golem hybrids.

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: You can't put them on the same tier.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: You keep your mouth shut. The last Restoration Core has been hidden in your stupid novel this whole time. All I can think about right now is landing a fist right in your face!

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: I'm ichorified. Your hand is the only thing that will hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: That's exactly why I haven't used my Guhua arts to hit you yet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, the paper people have become... um, solid people!

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: I can only say...

dialogues.speaker: Okikuni
dialogues.text: This feels SO good!

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: When was the last time I had a good stretch?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So how did you guys get turned into paper in the first place?

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Okikuni got so fired up reading the Liyue novels written by later generations that he wanted to dive in and join the adventure.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: He wanted to see if he had the strength of an entry-level Centurion... So he got turned into a paper person.

dialogues.speaker: Okikuni
dialogues.text: Cut it out. Be serious.

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: We've been swapping fun stories ever since we were selected to come here. Guess our earthly instincts never really left us, though, because we fell back into the habit of writing novels.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Though the relentless torment and tempering within the Apathic Interval sought to erode our will and desire, it somehow aligned with the ancient art of severing the Three Deadly Selves.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: But even if that tiny creative spark fades, a single good idea will suffice to bring it back to life.

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: Indeed. The Apathic Interval has stripped away my faith in Phobos, but I still get the urge to write every once in a while.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: And then, of course, we got punished by the guards. It's not hard to see why. Anyone who lays eyes on what Okikuni wrote can't help but exclaim...

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: "What's this weird stuff you're writing? But you know what, it's got a kick to it..."

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Mind you, it helps that the original work by those who came after in Liyue was excellent to begin with.

dialogues.speaker: Okikuni
dialogues.text: Don't rub it in. They'll start thinking that you're being serious.

dialogues.speaker: Okikuni
dialogues.text: Melanta classified our work as a pollutant. He claimed that it blurred the line between fact and fiction, sullying what should be a pure and proper cultural landscape.

dialogues.speaker: Okikuni
dialogues.text: Admittedly, our stories were shelved right alongside actual historical works and academic papers...

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: His principles are one thing, the stuff you write is another.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: By the way, Zeitlind, which of the five Yaksha generals do you like the most?

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Your sister read these stories with you when you were younger, right? She said Vritras was her favorite.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: We had already been pressed into a paper slip by the time she arrived, but she thought nothing of it and chatted with us for a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I like Alatus. He seems really strong and resilient. Neither my sister nor I could ever be as tough as he is.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just a side note, how do we restore this place and rescue the others?

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: What? That's hardly a "side note," it's serious business!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You could've fooled Paimon there with how much you're talking!

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: The thing that Dex just touched is the key. Whenever space is manipulated, it leaves a residual trail of its own reversal.

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: As for what it's called, we haven't given it a name yet. We'll have to come up with one, though, or it's going to be a pain to talk about.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: I think we should call it the "Ark-Key-ology Stone." We're digging through deep mysteries to unlock them. So, archeology, but with a key.

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: No, I'm all for "Hope-Key Dope-Key." It's more fitting. At the end of the day, hope is what remains within.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, this is such a hassle! The two of us are doing all the heavy lifting...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The three of us are doing all the heavy lifting, so we should get to name it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We'll call it the Restoration Core! No objections allowed!

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: I don't really mind. Once this place is completely liberated, we probably won't ever have to see it again.

dialogues.speaker: Okikuni
dialogues.text: I'd say it'd be best if nothing like it never exists again.

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: Fair enough. Well, you have our thanks for taking care of this.

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: Since the three of us, combined, barely have the strength of an entry-level rookie soldier, we'll sit this one out.

dialogues.speaker: Okikuni
dialogues.text: Heh. You've clearly overestimated yourself as a Remurian, just as you've overestimated the average strength of an average Remurian soldier.

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: The library entrance is right over there. With Dex's power, you should be able to find the hidden door in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You can return to the main hall in the center now. You'll be safe there. That's where Istoria and Josephus are waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: You guys get yourselves out of harm's way as planned. I will act as their guide for this leg of the journey.

dialogues.speaker: Calcerius
dialogues.text: Be careful! You haven't finished your novel yet.

dialogues.speaker: Okikuni
dialogues.text: We'll let everyone know we're safe, and then we'll come straight back. Please don't get turned into paper again.

talks.objective: Use Dex's ability to open the door to the library
Flip the pages to open the passage
Find a way to obtain the Restoration Core

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Istoria! You're here too!

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: That's right. Calcerius said that you stepped in at the Mahavaipulya Chamber. I suspect everything will fall into place from here on out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's too honesty from you, buster! Paimon's blushing already!

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Zeitlind, have you found what you've lost this time?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I have.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Speaking of which...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm here for my own reasons too.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: That's true. Since you came up here, you've done nothing but run around on my account...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I don't understand what the Watcher of Nothingness was saying, but I can tell that there's something in this place that matters to you.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}'s been a massive help. To hold up my end of the bargain, do tell me — what is it that you need?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: #You tell Istoria and Zeitlind about your experiences, and what Nihilita has said...\nYou ask if there are traces of your {M#sister}{F#brother} here.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: The story you speak of... It's simply incredible.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: If this were back in my academy days, I would have mulled over it for at least half a day before giving you an answer, just to prove I was taking you seriously.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: It's true that I've been here longer than anyone else, and I have witnessed all that has transpired. Unfortunately...

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: The highest point of the temple, the Atrium of Suchness, is where gods and Watchers dwell. It's said that certain hidden truths are kept within its walls.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: But hardly anyone is brave enough to set foot up there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you saying it's so, so high that even the most fearless would get scared?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Only those who choose to abandon all their memories are permitted to enter that hall.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: To seek an audience with the master of the temple is to seek answers and closure. It follows, then, that all memories that one gathers here shall be wiped away.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: One must construct the Path to the Heavens with their own memories and wisdom. Only then can they encounter the sacred beyond.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But memories aren't even solid! How are you supposed to build a path to the heavens with them?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Such is the nature of this place. The divine power of the gods can weave "emptiness" and "reality" into one another.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Here, mere vacuum is not perceived as nothingness. In the eyes of that being, it is a state that can be filled in the space of a single thought.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Only a "nothingness" where even meaning does not exist... Only that is a place beyond the reach of the gods.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: And I suspect that the Path to the Heavens should be similar to the half-real, half-illusory scenes that you saw in the library.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I'm just a coward at heart, after all. I never dared to make the climb. I simply don't have the courage to cast aside my responsibilities.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I am one who lived to witness what came before, and who continues to learn of what follows from those who come after. I am but a vessel for my precious memories.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Even if there is no hope of their ever returning to the surface, every lost civilization will live on in my memory.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Are gods really that horrid? To design such a cruel choice for someone to make...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Some gods are good, others are bad. Take the one who kidnapped {NICKNAME}'s {M#sister}{F#brother}, for instance. Totally bad!

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Perhaps it's the opposite. The god who designed the Path to the Heavens was not the mistress of the temple.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: You see, if you intend to leave this place, you simply cannot take its history, secrets or knowledge with you.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: The way I see it, the description of "using your memories to construct the Path to the Heavens" is too... emotionally charged.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Your memories are supposed to be wiped the moment you return to the mortal realm. But before that happens...

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: People here have the right to look back upon all they have ever been, all they have ever owned, and the path that results from both.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hold on. Let's see if Paimon got all that. It's like we've made a rule that says, you can read a book, but you have to chuck it into a fire the second you're done.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But just it all burns to a crisp, you find out the book has an epilogue and an afterword, where you get to look back at all the best parts.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: And then, in the end, nothing's left of the story. Only the feelings and impressions stay with you.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Spot on. A perfect read.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: You've got a real knack for analogies. Reminds me of one of my students, in fact. He went to Delphi Pytho.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I have no idea what it's called now, or if he survived the war.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: His name was Abrax, and while I've asked many people, no one has ever found his name in historical records.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Hmm. I went off on a tangent. Anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! You've said all that, but how do we get up there?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}'s memories are too important to forget.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #And as for Paimon, well, she hasn't clashed so hard with {NICKNAME} as to need a total reset.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: You don't have to worry.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Once we've rescued everyone, I'll help you with this. Actually, I've figured out how the Path to the Heavens works.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: The seat of the god has been left empty, so the rules have begun to falter. As such, a section of the Corridor of Nothingness's previous Path to the Heavens was preserved.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Melanta's fury destroyed half of it, but the remaining half, the stairway to heaven, is still vaguely visible.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: This means that the stairway can be used by others. We just have to make it whole again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, do you mean...

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Don't get the wrong idea. As I've said before, I am a coward burdened with too much memory, yet too scared to even die.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Istoria...

talks.objective: Flip through the pages and find a way to obtain the Restoration Core
Turn the pages to the scene of the library
Insert the Restoration Core and use Dex's ability to restore the space
Find a way to obtain the complete Restoration Core

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where's the last Restoration Core?

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: I believe it's hidden in this book.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: This book is called "Tale of the Lochknight Aerinny," Calcerius's translation of "Erinnyes."

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: It's more of a rewrite than a translation, though.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Istoria spoke very highly of it after his read. He said it captured the precise moment when realism collapsed into nominalism.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon has no idea what that means!

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I'd love to read it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay. Anyway, do you have any idea how we can retrieve the Restoration Core?

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: As I said before, we can use the power of this library to manifest scenes. The Restoration Core should be hidden in the book.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: #You'll need to enter the book and go on an adventure, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: It's time for you to experience what it's like to be a paper person, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But I'm a hero in three dimensions...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If anything happens, Paimon and Dex will come save you!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I need the greatest guide in Teyvat!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're unbelievable... Fine. Paimon will go with you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uncle Huangyi... This is super important, so don't mess up, 'kay?

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Actually, the restoration's success might rest entirely with Miss Zeitlind.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Melanta has reviewed and tampered with this text. It's filled with a great deal of unwarranted malice.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: And I'm too familiar with both "Aerinny" and the original "Erinnyes." My heart lacks the power to alter the scenes in time.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Put another way, my perception of this story is irrevocably locked on its tragedy. But it must be rewritten to have a happy ending.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what do we do?

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: We'll need Zeitlind to neutralize every crisis that emerges in the text, then steer the plot toward a happy ending...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Are you really going to put their safety in my hands?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: And you even want me to imagine good things happening out of the blue...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I can't do it. I can't do anything right.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We believe in you!

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: We aren't just "living," we're adventuring! Fortune favors the bold, you know. Heaven helps those who help themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: ...Alright. I'll try.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, it's a trap!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zeitlind, are you okay? That was a nasty fall!

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} had my back. I was a little scared, but I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I'm sorry. I keep dragging you down...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No you don't!

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Well, I know I'm dead weight. No one so much as gave a hoot about little ol' me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Whaddayamean? Didn't Paimon grab onto you and {NICKNAME} just now?

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: You weren't pulling us upwards! You were using me as a buffer!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Pfft. Uncle Huangyi, Paimon can fly. She wouldn't even have fallen if she wasn't trying to help you and {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, alright. It's all my fault for being so heavy, I guess.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Heh.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zeitlind smiled! We make a great team, Uncle Huangyi!

dialogues.speaker: Yu Huangyi
dialogues.text: Don't wind yourself up too tight, Zeitlind.

talks.objective: Find the other half of the Restoration Core
Insert the Restoration Core and use Dex's ability to restore the space

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew. That was a... unique experience.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How are you feeling?

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: No need to thank me. The stakes were much higher for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dex seems to be really interested in this thing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This has to be how we restore them to their former selves, right?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: A lifetime spent here... I think I could be content with that.
